items.stem: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?

options.rationale: Correct: HAVING filters rows produced after GROUP BY aggregation.
WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.
ORDER BY sorts the final result; it does not filter groups.
LIMIT caps the number of returned rows; it does not filter groups.

items.explanation: Correct: HAVING applies conditions to aggregated groups, unlike WHERE which filters rows first.

items.stem: Which TWO join results keep rows from the left table even when there is no matching right-table row? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: a LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows, filling unmatched right columns with NULL.
Correct: a FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both sides, including the left.
An INNER JOIN drops left rows that have no match.
A CROSS JOIN pairs every row with every other row; it is not match-based.

items.explanation: Correct: LEFT JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN both preserve unmatched left-table rows.

items.stem: How does a window function differ from a GROUP BY aggregate?

options.text: It returns a value per row without collapsing the rows
options.rationale: Correct: window functions compute across a set but keep every input row.

options.text: It always sorts the table permanently
options.rationale: Window functions do not permanently sort stored data.

options.text: It can only be used on primary keys
options.rationale: Window functions apply to any columns, not just keys.
Window functions do not deduplicate rows.

items.explanation: Correct: a window function produces a result for each row rather than collapsing groups.
